data.name: Corona Blossom Vol.1 Gift From the Galaxy
data.detailed_description:
"Corona Blossom" is a visual novel.
(A kinetic novel, without any choices)

The game features character art and designs by artist nanaca mai, who previously worked on the super deformed character art in "The Fruit of Grisaia."
Now, her cute characters will come to life, moving and expressing their emotions using the "e-mote" system.

STORY:
Meet Keiji Osaki: a young man who hates dealing with machines, despite being very skilled at working with them. That's just the kind of guy he is.
After failing his college entrance exams, he begins helping out at his grandfather's workshop, which specializes in repairing VORKS, heavy-duty industrial robots. For a while, he enjoyed a quiet life in the countryside, doted on by the workshop's regular patrons.
One day, however, his life suddenly takes a turn for the strange, when he encounters a metallic lifeform attached to a meteorite that fell from the sky.
To make things even more complicated, the organism he rescues takes the form of a forgotten girl from his past. This is how his life with the metallic organism known as R-ne begins. But after a while, R-ne learns how to speak, and tells Keiji that she wants to go back to her home planet. Moved by her words, he sets his mind on sending her back into space, no matter what.
This may prove difficult, though, when a female space pirate - also known as a rare metal hunter - appears out of nowhere, and gets in his way.
Caught up in this whirlwind, will Keiji and his friends be able to send R-ne safely back to her homeland?

data.short_description: Meet R-ne, a metallic organism from space in the form of a young girl. She’s taken in by Keiji and the people of Hanma town, but the maid uniform-clad, cat-eared space pirate Lily and her crew are looking to sell the valuable metal that’s R-ne. Caught up in the turmoil, can she make it back home?

reviews.review:
Corona Blossom Vol. 1 Gift From the Galaxy follows Keiji Oosaki, a guy who works with machines at his grandfather's workshop. One day, he and his friends come across a metal blob that takes the form of a girl. Not long after, they name the girl R-ne. As she learns new things, Keiji's life continues to change. 

As the first VN in a trilogy, Gift From the Galaxy needs to get you comfortable with the setting and plot. Additionally, it needs to establish the characters and their relationships without feeling like the plot did not do enough. In my eyes, it succeeded. Throughout the moments of slice-of-life and comedy, we get some surprisingly sweet character moments here and there. Out of this VN's likable cast of characters, Keiji and R-ne are the most notable ones here. With Keiji, you learn many things about him like his motivations and why he works with machines despite hating them. The latter was explained in a very touching part of the story. In the end, you cannot help but admire him. As for R-ne, it was fun seeing her slowly grow into her own person. At first, I thought it was a missed opportunity to skip seeing R-ne speak for the first time. Thankfully, the story has many scenes showing R-ne learning things, so it did not bother me. It all meshes together to create an enjoyable story with an ending that gets you excited for the next part of the series. 

A good story is nice and all, but what about the visuals and music? I can say that they are good here. With the E-mote system, the sprites are animated almost flawlessly. The way they go from different expressions and mouth sprites never gets tiring to look at. There was a moment in Chapter 3 where Shino's mouth animations were bugging out, though. Aside from the sprites, the backgrounds and CGs look great, utilizing colors and lighting nicely. They even put in the effort of animating some effects during the chibi CGs. As for the music, Corona Blossom Volume 1 has a solid soundtrack with nice variety, allowing each song to fit whatever scene they are used in. While there are a bunch of relaxing songs, the soundtrack also includes some tense songs, too. The OP is alright, but it will take a bunch of more times listening to it for me to REALLY like it. The same cannot be said about the ED, which combines some soothing vocals and instruments to create a fitting tune to listen to during the credits.

Overall, Corona Blossom Volume is a good visual novel that succeeded in getting me to care about its world, story, and characters. Its mostly lighthearted story and plot make the more serious moments leave a more lasting impact. I always love it whenever a visual novel can perfectly place moments like those between many slice-of-life scenes. If my only problem with this VN is the lip-sync animation messing up at a few points, then this series is off to a good start. I cannot wait to see what's in store for me in Volume 2.
